name: Turn Order: Time Track
description: A turn order mechanism where players' actions cost a certain amount of 'time'. When a player takes an action, their marker advances on a time track by the amount of time spent. The player whose marker is furthest behind on the time track is generally the next player to take a turn. This allows for multiple actions by one player if they take short actions, while longer actions push their marker further ahead, delaying their next turn.

parameters.name: Time Cost of Actions
parameters.description: How much 'time' each available action costs. Can be fixed per action type or variable.

parameters.name: Track Length / Reset
parameters.description: Is the time track finite? Does it loop or reset? What happens when markers reach the end?
parameters.default_value: Finite track, may trigger end of round or game

parameters.name: Tie-breaking on Track
parameters.description: If multiple player markers are on the same time space, who goes next (e.g., player who arrived last, fixed tie-breaker token, player on top of a stack).
parameters.default_value: Player who arrived last on the space (or is on top if stacked)

parameters.name: Bonus Spaces/Events on Track
parameters.description: Are there specific spaces on the time track that grant bonuses, trigger events, or provide income when landed on or passed?

examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Players move on a central time board. The player furthest behind always takes the next turn. Moving to get a patch costs time shown on the board.
Players move along a linear track. The player furthest behind on the track takes the next turn, moving to any open action space ahead of them.

examples_in_games.game_name: Glen More / Glen More II: Chronicles
examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: Players move their marker around a track of tiles. The player furthest behind takes the next turn, choosing a tile ahead of their marker. The distance moved determines how many tiles are 'passed over' and removed.
Players spend weeks (time) to travel and excavate. The player who has spent the least amount of time overall takes the next turn.

Players move around a central board, and actions/resources cost varying amounts of 'time' (movement on a score track that also acts as a time track). The player furthest behind on this track typically plays next.

notes_on_combination_modification: Time track turn order creates interesting dilemmas about taking multiple small turns versus a single powerful but time-consuming turn. It can be self-balancing as players who fall behind get more turns. The 'cost' of time for actions is the critical tuning knob for this mechanic.
